title.analysis: 'Actually Fixing Your Money in 6 Months' makes a bounded process promise rather than an extreme wealth fantasy. 'Actually' challenges ineffective prior efforts; the six-month unit gives the viewer a concrete planning horizon.
title.script_alignment: Cold open shows a frictionless card tap, then rewinds to 6:47 a.m. and nine days of balance avoidance. Month one inventories four spending piles and $530 unworn shoes; month two starts $60 savings; month three chooses snowball motivation, sells the shoes for $220 and skips Nashville. Month four redirects a hypothetical $549 BMW lease into a Roth; month five asks for 8% and gets 6%; month six automates transfers and sketches a St Petersburg condo goal. Circular phone-check ending reinforces emotional relief. The abrupt 'Marcus, no... Grant' correction and final unfinished question remain visible in stored ASR.

title.analysis: $1.8 Billion supplies extreme aspiration, 'in Silence' adds secrecy and 'First in Your Family' adds an intergenerational identity stake. Unlike a generic billionaire-advice promise, the viewer is the protagonist.
title.script_alignment: Starts behind a Queens restaurant at 11:43 p.m. with dish-station hands and folded margin calculations. Parents' $340 and a coffee-tin emergency fund establish inherited scarcity. A failed $1,500 launch leaves $23.17; websites grow to a $6,800 monthly agency, then software, a rejected VC offer and $10.1M ARR. Tax surprise and cousin Darnell's rent request introduce new burdens; Jerome's fading calls dramatize social distance. At 47, a Forbes call confirms $1.84B; helping Maya with exponents resolves the opening's family ceiling emotionally. Repeated radiator/coffee-tin motifs hold the long arc, while business scale between ARR and billionaire valuation remains undescribed.

script.claim_audit: The script says 'this year' 401k $23,500 and IRA $7,000, whereas the official pre-upload IRS 2026 notice specifies $24,500 and $7,500. This is a year-context mismatch, not proof the whole mechanism fails. Paycheck-to-paycheck figures and retirement average/median lack sources and denominators. Homeowner-versus-renter wealth is an observational comparison; the script cannot establish buying causes that gap. Routing the full gross $12K raise to savings omits taxes; balance/expense feasibility is not reconciled. Location moves from Tulsa mechanic to Texas house without an explicit relocation bridge.
script.ending_words: The quiet was never the absence of something. It was the thing itself, working the whole time. You go inside. The light's still off in the kitchen. You'll find the switch eventually.
